policy.rule: Treat this file as a dated incident-response baseline. Re-check primary sources before version-specific remediation or legal conclusions.
policy.no_absolute_clean_claim: Use 'No known indicators were found within the examined scope as of [timestamp]' instead of claiming that a site is absolutely clean.
policy.preferred_recovery: For confirmed compromise, prefer a trusted rebuild or a verified isolated restore over an unproven in-place cleanup.

components.verified_fact: WordPress 7.0.2 is the latest release in the 7.0 series and was released on 2026-07-17.
components.security_context: The release addresses one critical and one high-severity security issue, and forced auto-updates were enabled for affected sites.

components.verified_fact: Only the most recent release in the 7.0 series is identified as safe to use and actively maintained in the release archive.
WordPress 7.1 is scheduled for 2026-08-19, but beta and release-candidate builds are not production recovery targets.
WordPress recommends PHP 8.3 or greater, MariaDB 10.11 or greater or MySQL 8.0 or greater, an Nginx or Apache environment with rewrite support, and HTTPS.
components.legacy_warning: Compatibility minimums are not security recommendations; EOL PHP or database versions remain unacceptable long-term targets.

components.verified_fact: PHP 8.2, 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 are supported on the verification date. PHP 8.2 and 8.3 receive security fixes only; PHP 8.4 and 8.5 remain in active support.
Only the latest WordPress version is officially supported; the security team may backport critical fixes to older versions as a courtesy.
Official hardening guidance covers trusted download sources, encrypted administration, permissions, wp-config protection, file editing, backups, logging and monitoring.
Official hacked-site guidance emphasizes identifying indicators of compromise, changing access credentials, comparing files with official sources and taking a pragmatic incident-response approach.
wp core verify-checksums compares installed core files with WordPress.org checksums and runs before WordPress loads.
components.limitation: Checksum success does not examine uploads, database content, MU plugins, custom/premium code, host persistence, control planes or third-party scripts.

components.verified_fact: wp plugin verify-checksums verifies WordPress.org-hosted plugin files where checksums are available.
components.limitation: Premium, custom, removed or otherwise unverifiable packages require independent provenance and comparison.

components.verified_fact: WordPress can apply minor/security background updates, and the security team can trigger plugin/theme updates for critical cases; configuration may still disable those mechanisms.
Changing WordPress secret keys and salts invalidates existing authentication cookies.
Application Passwords are revocable per-application credentials for programmatic WordPress API access and must be inventoried during identity response.
NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3, published in April 2025, integrates incident response recommendations into cybersecurity risk management aligned with CSF 2.0.
